text:
incident-bot: [PAGER] Private cluster autoscaler entering backoff — GPU node provisioning failing for customer GlobalRetailOps (vpc-PRD-3). Queue depth growing for inference service 'inference/gentext' and requests being throttled.
Alex: Paging SRE oncall. I see queue size 8.2k, OOM throttles on the autoscaler, and a slew of bootstrap timeouts.
Joan: On it. Any immediate customer-visible errors?
Ana: CS reports increased 429s and latency spikes. Customer noticed failed deployments and timeouts since ~09:12 UTC.
Lee: Tagging infra. What's the autoscaler error logs showing?
Ravi: From logs: 
```
2026-03-15T09:10:43Z autoscaler: scaling event failed: capacity_exhausted: requested_gpus=64, allocatable=32
2026-03-15T09:11:02Z node-bootstrap: timeout waiting for kubelet: node=prv-node-xx, reason=failed-attach
2026-03-15T09:12:28Z autoscaler: backoff until 2026-03-15T09:22:28Z
```
Alex: So autoscaler is hitting customer cluster limits and node attach timeouts. Could be image pull or firewall issue.
Joan: I'm running quick checks: `kubectl get nodes -w` shows a bunch of Provisioning nodes stuck in 'NotReady' and many Pending pods with `FailedAttachVolume` and `node controller` events.
Lee: Can someone check customer VPC quotas and route table association? If ENIs can't attach, that would explain attach failures.
Ana: Customer says they made a recent networking change to their VPC (added extra NACL rules) around 08:55 UTC.
Ravi: Workaround: we can temporarily scale the request routing to a lower GPU SKU (1/2 batch) or route to hosted fallback pool to reduce load on the private cluster. Recommend switching canary for affected prod route.
Alex: Agreed. Joan — can you flip traffic to hosted-fallback for the next 30m to drain the queue? I'll open a mitigation runbook and notify the customer.
Joan: Doing now. Command:
```
# switch route to fallback
redwoodctl routes update inference/gentext --pool hosted-fallback --weight 100
```
Joan: Confirmed: routing change applied. Queue dropped from 8.2k -> 600 over 6 minutes.
Ana: I told GlobalRetailOps support we've routed their traffic to fallback and are investigating root cause. They want ETA.
Lee: I'll start debugging node bootstrap logs with the customer's cloud console. Initial hypothesis: customer's VPC change blocked metadata or attach traffic causing `aws-attach` failures.
Ravi: Also enabling a temporary autoscaler override to increase retry attempts and reduce backoff so we don't stall on partial failures.
Alex: Go for it, but watch cost. Joan, keep monitoring latency and 429s.
Joan: Latency normalized on fallback, 429s down to baseline. Still seeing Node bootstrap timeouts in private cluster:
```
Mar 15 09:11:05 kubelet[1234]: ErrImagePull: Get "https://registry.example.com/v2/": dial tcp 203.0.113.12:443: i/o timeout
```
Lee: That points to egress/route issues. Customer's NACL change likely blocking access to registry or control plane.
Ana: Customer now acknowledges they pushed a NACL change and are reverting. They estimate 10-15m to revert.
Alex: Handoff plan: Joan remains primary for mitigation and monitoring for next 30m; Lee is owner for deep-dive on node provisioning; Ravi will follow up on autoscaler backoff logic and add a failover path; Ana to coordinate customer comms. I'll escalate to eng-runtime if we see reoccurrence after revert.
Joan: I'll keep updates here. Current metrics: queue 120, p50 latency 160ms, 429s traceable to prior 2k reqs in log.
Lee: Started capture of bootstrap logs and ENI attach attempts; captured packet drops to 203.0.113.0/24 from customer NACL.
Ravi: Created follow-up issue #INF-4826 to add better autoscaler observability + fast-fail policy when node-attach consistently fails.
Alex: Thanks team. @Ana please update customer with the change window and confirm when NACL is reverted.
Ana: Will do. (cc @GlobalRetailOps)
deploy-bot: Deployment check — no new releases to affected service in last 24h.
Joan: handing off 30m monitor to Lee. I'm logging the mitigation steps and will annotate the incident at conclusion. :white_check_mark: 
Lee: Acknowledged — taking over monitoring for next shift. Will post a postmortem once we have root cause and timeline.
IncidentBot: Incident acknowledged and tagged for postmortem tracking (owner=Lee, sev=2, incident_id=INC-20260315-87).
